messages:
sam.dev: Heads-up — we're getting multiple reports that the JS SDK sample app  (next+edge) breaks on deploy with 'TypeError: require is not defined'. Looks like our dual-pkg conditional exports aren't behaving well in edge runtimes. Anyone seen this in the wild?

maria.dx: Yep saw 2 threads today. Vercel Edge logs show stack starting in our shipped dist/index.cjs shim. Edge runtimes (Cloudflare/Vercel/Deno) don't support require, so the CJS entrypoint gets picked by bundlers sometimes and dies.

alex.sdk: Repro steps (local edge build): `npm pack` then install into a next-edge app, deploy — runtime error. Locally swapping import to `import * as R from '@redwood/inference'` then `R.default` works in some bundlers but not consistent.

josh.build: Short note: our package.json currently has this exports block: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
and top-level "main" points to dist/index.cjs and "module" to dist/index.mjs. That combo confuses older bundlers and edge toolchains.

toni.eng: Also, TypeScript users reported their editors failed to find typings unless package.json has a top-level "types" field. Our current types only via exports condition doesn't always get picked up by tsserver.

maria.dx: UX hits: onboarding sample uses require() in examples for older Node tutorials, so new users copy that into edge projects and explode. We need to update sample app and docs asap.

alex.sdk: Options I see: (1) Keep dual-pkg but change exports to prefer import for default condition shapes (node/import->mjs, default->mjs) and only expose a tiny CJS shim under a condition so bundlers don't choose it for edge, (2) Publish ESM-only + a generated compat CJS package_name.cjs for node consumers, (3) Move to single ESM build + provide a separate package e.g., @redwood/inference-cjs with CJS wrapper.

josh.build: FWIW bundlers pick entry by algorithm: top-level exports+main/module/types matter. Edge deployers often use esbuild/rollup which prefer ESM but the local dev bundler we test with picks main for some reason.

sam.dev: Can we try a minimal change that reduces breakage? Maybe swap to exports with explicit conditions that avoid providing "require" for non-node environments. Example suggestion: 
```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./node": { "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "default": "./dist/index.mjs"
}
```
But not sure if that syntax validates for bundlers.

toni.eng: Also add top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" — fixes editor lookups quickly. We should add "types" even if we keep conditional types in exports.

alex.sdk: For typings entrypoints, TS prefers top-level "types" for convenience, but consumers using path mapping to get subpath types need explicit exports pointing to .d.ts as well. So do both.

maria.dx: Actionable DX fixes: update sample app to ESM import examples, add an "edge-debugging" note in onboarding, publish a canary with changed exports, and add CI jobs that test install+run on Vercel Edge & Cloudflare Workers runtime images.

josh.build: I can draft a minimal exports change and a CJS shim that is only included under a "node" condition. Then publish a canary tag. I'll also add a simple smoke test in release pipeline that runs the Next edge sample.

sam.dev: Nice. One more thing — let's ensure our README & quickstart snippets are ESM-first. Lots of people copy/paste.

toni.eng: I'll open a docs PR to convert examples + add a note about types field.

alex.sdk: For long-term: consider single ESM distribution + separate compatibility package. Easier for edge-first ecosystem. But that is a bigger breaking bump.

maria.dx: Agreed. Short-term canary + docs + sample fix. Long-term RFC for publishing strategy (ESM-primary + opt-in CJS compat) — capture perf, bundle size, and customer compatibility trade-offs.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist — triggered smoke tests on branch. Results will post in this thread. :rocket:

sam.dev: Cool. Thanks team — josh, can you post the canary package name here when ready so devex can test with the sample?

josh.build: Will do. Targeting a canary by EOD.

maria.dx: I'll coordinate with product marketing to update the quickstart page once canary is stable. :+1:
